summary.text: Ben Ming is a Democratic candidate for the New Hampshire House of Representatives, Hillsborough 35, in the November 3, 2026 general election. He represented the same district from 2022 to 2024.

paragraphs.text: Ben Ming earned a B.S. in computer science from The George Washington University in 2003, an A.L.M. in information technology with a concentration in software engineering from Harvard University, and a J.D. from Suffolk University Law School, according to Ballotpedia.
Ballotpedia lists his career experience as including work as an attorney.
Ming ran for New Hampshire House of Representatives Hillsborough 40 in 2020, when Keith Ammon defeated him.
In 2022 he and incumbent Kat McGhee defeated Liz Barbour and incumbent Susan Homola in the general election for Hillsborough 35.

He assumed office on December 7, 2022 and left office on December 4, 2024, and Ballotpedia lists him on the House Judiciary Committee and the Fish and Game and Marine Resources Committee for 2023-2024.
In 2024 he was the Democratic candidate for New Hampshire State Senate District 12, losing to incumbent Kevin Avard, 55.9% to 44.1%.
